## Triage — `finding` promoted · `domain:devx` · `pm:queue` · `priority:p2` · type **Bug**

⚠️ **STAND-IN TRIAGE, declared.** `domain:devx @ objectui` execution seat (`session_013VGeMu3p6qEFWR6K6GGLaW`, R58), under 〈多仓协调〉规则 4's stand-in clause. Vacancy read, ⛔ not assumed: triage seat objectstack#6015 filed a **shift-close brief 2026-09-14T05:50:56Z** on the maintainer's order, with no later round-open marker. ⛔ I stop the moment that seat is taken.

### ⚠️ A conflict of interest I am declaring rather than hiding

This routing puts the card **into my own lane**. `.github/workflows/changeset-release.yml` is 「构建与发布管线」, which `references/lanes/devx.md` names as this seat's surface, so I believe it is simply correct — but a stand-in triage decision that hands work to the seat making it deserves to be visible. ⇒ ⭐ **the incoming triage seat should re-read this routing specifically**, and overturning it costs nothing.

### Classification: class (a), ⛔ not a judgement call

「可复现缺陷(复现或失败探针)」 — 25 of 25 scheduled runs failed at one named step with 63 assertion failures and **zero** timeouts, and the `push` leg of the same workflow file is 17/17 green. That is a reproducible defect with a named location and a firing control. ⇒ promoted, `finding` stripped.

### type = **Bug**

The step **declares** it validates the post-version tree and instead fails against it on every run. ⛔ Not Task, ⛔ not Feature — nothing widens.

### Why `p2` and not `p1` — and the exact trigger that would move it

⭐ **A reading I took while grading this, which the card does not contain and which raises the stakes:**

| reading | value |
|:--|:--|
| latest GitHub release | **`@object-ui/*@17.5.0`, published 2026-08-14** — a month ago |
| in-tree version (`packages/i18n/package.json`) | **17.6.0** |
| open Version Packages PR | **objectui#5400** `chore: release packages`, head `changeset-release/main` — **last updated 2026-09-07T12:17:11Z** |
| scheduled `Changeset Release` lane | failing since **2026-09-08T06:13Z**, 25/25 |

⇒ the release PR went stale **the day before** this lane started failing, and nothing has been published for a month.

⛔ **I am NOT claiming causation, and the correlation is not proof.** The mechanism that would refresh objectui#5400 is in the failing workflow, so "this red is why the release train is stopped" is the *obvious* reading — and obvious readings on this card's subject are exactly what the last two days of this lane's errata are about. It is a **hypothesis with a date that lines up**, ⛔ not a measurement.

⭐ **Mechanical re-grade trigger — raise to `p1` the moment either holds:**
1. anyone establishes that the `Validate the post-version tree` failure is what keeps objectui#5400 from refreshing; **or**
2. a merged fix on `main` is named that users cannot get because nothing has published since 2026-08-14.

⇒ **p2 today** because nothing here yet names a user who is blocked; **p1 immediately** once (1) or (2) is measured.

### ⛔ Fences for whoever takes this — this lane may NOT run a release

`references/lanes/devx.md` is explicit: 「⛔ 不做任何发布动作,含改根 `version` 脚本链;能点绿的门禁不等于该点绿」, and release is human-only.

- ✅ **In scope**: diagnosing *why* `Validate the post-version tree` asserts, and repairing the validation or the thing it correctly objects to.
- ⛔ **Out of scope**: running a release, merging or refreshing objectui#5400, touching the root `version` script chain, or `content/docs/releases/**`.
- ⛔ **Above all**: ⛔ do not make the assertion pass by weakening it. 63 assertion failures with zero flakes is a validator that may well be **telling the truth about a real defect in the post-version tree**. ⭐ Establish which of the two it is — a wrong validator, or a right validator objecting to a genuinely broken tree — **before** proposing any repair. Getting that backwards here would silence a release-blocking check.

⚠️ Also on the record: this and objectui#9271 are **disjoint** — no shared site, and 9271's window is 195 timeouts / 0 assertion failures while this one is 63 assertion failures / 0 timeouts. ⛔ Do not fold them.

| 10 most recent `changeset-release.yml` runs, `branch=main event=schedule` | **10 / 10 `failure`** |

⇒ the control fires on the same workflow, so ⛔ this is not a broken reader and the schedule/push asymmetry is real. The card's own census (25/25 scheduled failures since 2026-09-08, **63 assertion failures, zero timeouts**) is ⛔ not something you need to re-derive.

## ⭐ Zone 1 — RULINGS, ⛔ not re-openable by you

1. ⛔⛔ **DO NOT make the assertion pass by weakening it.** 63 assertion failures with **zero** flakes across six days is the signature of a validator that may well be **telling the truth about a genuinely broken post-version tree**. ⭐ **Your first deliverable is to establish which of the two it is** — a wrong validator, or a right validator objecting to a real defect — **before proposing any repair at all.** Getting that backwards would silence a release-blocking check, which is the worst outcome available here.
2. ⛔ **This lane runs NO release actions.** `references/lanes/devx.md`: 「⛔ 不做任何发布动作,含改根 `version` 脚本链」. ⇒ ⛔ do not run a release, ⛔ do not touch or refresh the standing Version Packages PR objectui#5400, ⛔ do not touch the root `version` script chain, ⛔ never touch `content/docs/releases/**`.
3. ⛔ **Do not make the lane non-blocking, do not disable the schedule, do not add `continue-on-error`.** "Stop the alarm" is not a repair.

## Zone 2 — PM mechanism assumptions (⭐ measure these; I expect at least one to be wrong)

- **A.** I assume the schedule/push asymmetry is because the two triggers take **different paths** through this workflow — most likely the scheduled run performs a version bump and then validates the resulting tree, while the push leg never reaches that step. ⭐ **Verify it.** If the push leg simply *skips* the step, then "the push leg is green" says nothing about the tree and the card's control is weaker than it looks.
- **B.** I assume the 63 assertion failures are one repeated assertion rather than 63 distinct ones. ⛔ Unverified — read them.

## Zone 3 — context you may use, ⛔ not a conclusion

While grading this I measured three things that line up in time. ⛔ **I did NOT establish causation and you should not assume it:**

- last GitHub release: **`@object-ui/*@17.5.0`, 2026-08-14** — a month ago; in-tree is `17.6.0`
- the open Version Packages PR objectui#5400 has not updated since **2026-09-07T12:17Z**
- this lane has failed since **2026-09-08T06:13Z**

⇒ the obvious reading is "this red is why nothing publishes". ⭐ **It is a hypothesis with dates that line up, nothing more** — and if your diagnosis happens to confirm or refute it, say so explicitly, because it decides this card's priority (a written trigger raises it to p1 if confirmed).

## Acceptance

1. **The verdict, stated plainly**: is `Validate the post-version tree` wrong, or is the post-version tree wrong? With the reading that decides it.
2. The failing assertion(s) quoted from a real run, with the population named (how many distinct assertions, not just "63").
3. Zone 2 A answered: what the push leg actually does at that step.
4. Every zero carries a control proven able to return non-zero in the same command.
5. `gates_weakened:` must read **NONE**, or name exactly what was weakened and the measurement showing it was the correct repair.

## ⭐ An explicitly acceptable — and possibly preferred — outcome

⛔ **Do not force a PR.** If the diagnosis lands and the repair turns out to touch release machinery, or to be a product/release decision, then **`premise_still_valid: true` + the verdict + a named fork, with NO PR, is a complete and welcome delivery.** ⭐ Reporting "the validator is right and here is what is actually broken" would be the single most valuable thing this card can produce, and it is explicitly not a failure to stop there.

⛔ Deliver a **DRAFT PR** if and only if the repair is squarely inside this lane. ⛔ Never flip ready, enqueue, or arm auto-merge. Post your structured JSON report as a comment on **objectui#9472** first.

⛔ Never measure on the shared checkout `/home/user/objectui`. ⚠️ This container may be a shallow clone (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`); if so `git log -S` gives only false negatives. ⚠️ The job-log blob host has been refused by two sibling seats' egress — check whether yours can reach it before assuming, and say which you found.

## The verdict, plainly

**`Validate the post-version tree` is not wrong. It is telling the truth about a post-version tree that is genuinely broken — for 48 of the 63 assertion annotations. A second, smaller cause (7 of 63) is the opposite: a test asking a question that cannot hold after a version bump. Those two must not be repaired the same way.**

### The reading that decides it

`packages/components/src/index.css` line 1 is a bare `@import 'tailwindcss';`. It is the **only one of this repo's four stylesheet entries without `source(none)`** — `fields`, `plugin-grid` and `plugin-kanban` all carry it, and their own comments name components' entry as the one that leaves detection on. So Tailwind v4 automatic source detection is active for components, rooted at `packages/components/`, and it scans `CHANGELOG.md` (473 kB of prose, and a published file — it is in that package's `files[]`).

`pnpm changeset:version` writes each pending changeset body into the CHANGELOG of every package its frontmatter names. `.changeset/8506-detail-placeholders-shared-empty-value.md` names `'@object-ui/components': patch` and its body contains, verbatim:

    - Both retire their own `text-muted-foreground/60 text-sm` treatment and take the

Run that version step and `packages/components/CHANGELOG.md` gains that line (measured: 1 occurrence; a control token planted the same way: 0). Prose becomes a real utility in components' sheet. The plugin builders subtract whatever components already ships. So the class leaves `@object-ui/plugin-kanban`'s sheet — while `packages/plugin-kanban/src/KanbanImpl.tsx:492` still emits it on the empty-column placeholder.

### What that ships

Built plugin-kanban's sheet through its own builder, control and mutation in one command:

| leg | build | classes | `.text-muted-foreground/60` in sheet | `.bg-card/60` (probe control) |
|:--|:--|--:|:--|:--|
| components CHANGELOG as on `main` | SUCCEEDED | 59 | **present** | present |
| one prose line added, as the version step will write it | **SUCCEEDED** | 58 | **gone** | present |

The build does **not** throw, because `text-muted-foreground/60` is not in plugin-kanban's `MUST_SURVIVE`. That is the builder's own named failure mode: "That is over-subtraction, and it ships as an under-styled package with a green build." The validator is the only thing that catches it.

⚠️ The sharper version: `bg-card/60` **is** in `MUST_SURVIVE`. Ablation leg POS2 planted that class in the CHANGELOG and the test went red too — the day a changeset body mentions it, the release build stops being silently wrong and starts failing outright.

### The workflow's own premise is false

The design note above the step (`changeset-release.yml`, the block starting "WHY THIS IS NOT `pnpm test`") argues:

> THE VERSION STEP CANNOT MOVE A SOURCE BYTE. ... Zero `.ts`, zero `.tsx`, zero config. The source in the post-version tree is byte-identical to the `main` commit this run checked out

**A generated `CHANGELOG.md` is a stylesheet source byte.** The enumeration of the four path kinds is correct; the conclusion drawn from it is not.

## The population, named

25 most recent `event=schedule` runs of workflow 223783348 on `main` (run numbers 5171 to 5630), every failing job's every check-run annotation fetched: **88 annotations = 63 `AssertionError` + 25 runner `Process completed with exit code 1`, 0 timeouts**. Those 63 are **6 distinct (file, line, first message line) sites**, not 63 and not 1:
